info.title: Lustro Screen debug tab
info.description: The app's windows and the UI tree in each: the classic Views, and the Compose semantics nodes of each Compose host, read in the app's process on the main thread. A read takes milliseconds, sees every test tag, and does not wait for the screen to stop changing, as uiautomator dump does; ?settle waits for two reads in a row to be the same, with the window focus at rest. The tree has the app's own windows only: a permission dialog, the chooser, the keyboard, a notification, and a toast are not in it, and a WebView is a View without its page. When no window has hasWindowFocus, a window of another app is on top. The text of a password field comes as one dot for each character. From 1.1, POST click, set-text, and scroll run a node's semantics action, found by its test tag, text, content description, or id, as the app's own code: they do no hit-testing, and they act only on a node that a user can reach, in the window that has the focus and with a part on the screen, unless the body says force. The tab has no console view, so it is not in the tab bar; _meta lists it. All routes are token-authenticated (Bearer header or HttpOnly cookie) and live under /api/v1/screen. Errors use the shared error envelope.

servers.description: The Lustro debug server (loopback by default).

get.summary: The app's windows, and the nodes of each.
get.description: Reads every window of the app's process on the main thread, and calls the app's ScreenContextProvider after the read. GET changes nothing. When the main thread does not start the read in 5000 ms, or does not finish it in 5000 ms and the settle time, the request answers 504 with code main_thread_blocked. When the read throws, as with a View of the app whose getter throws, it answers 500 with code read_failed, and the app goes on.

parameters.name: merged
parameters.description: true for the merged semantics tree, in which a clickable node carries the text of its children, as accessibility services see it; false for the unmerged one, in which each text is a node of its own. A node has the same id in both. 400 with field merged for any other value.

parameters.name: settle
parameters.description: Read the tree on each frame until two reads in a row are the same and the window focus is at rest, the top visible window that can take the focus having it and no other window, for up to this many milliseconds, and return the last read with settle. The window manager moves the focus some frames after a dialog opens or closes. 0 reads once. 400 with field settle for any other value.

post.description: Runs the OnClick semantics action of a Compose node, or performClick() of a View, on the main thread, then reads the tree. The selector looks in the unmerged tree, so a test tag or a text inside a clickable parent is found, and the action runs on the matched node or the nearest node above it that has it, as a tap on the text would. It acts as a user can, unless force is true: only in the window that has the focus and in the popups over it, such as a menu, which take no focus but get the touches inside them, also a popup that a popup with the focus opened, and only on a target with a part on the screen. Before it looks, it waits for the next frame, and then up to 500 ms for the window focus to come to rest: a Compose dialog comes on the frame after the tap that opened it, and the focus reaches a new dialog some frames later. 404 with code no_match when no node matches. 409 with code ambiguous when nodes with different targets match, with the candidates' ids in the message; not_in_focused_window when the node is only in a window that does not have the focus and is not a popup on the one that has it, such as the activity under a dialog; no_window_focus when no window of the app has the focus, as with a permission dialog on top; not_on_screen when the target has no part on the screen; disabled when the target is disabled; and no_action when neither the node nor a node above it has the action. 500 with code action_failed when the app's action throws. 400 with the key as field for a key that the route does not take, two selectors, or a value of the wrong type. The action does no hit-testing: to check what a user can do, tap the middle of the node's visibleBounds with adb shell input tap instead.

text.description: A text of the node, exactly, or its editable text.

contentDescription.description: A content description of the node, exactly.

id.description: The node's id from GET tree.

force.description: Act also on a node that a user can't tap now: in a window that does not have the focus and is not a popup on the one that has it, such as the activity under a dialog, or with no part on the screen. By default the tab refuses them.

merged.description: The tree of the response, merged or unmerged.

settle.description: After the action, read the tree on each frame from the next one until two reads in a row are the same and the window focus is at rest, for up to this many milliseconds, at least two frames: an animation that the action starts, such as a Compose scroll, moves nothing on its first frame.

post.summary: Replace the text of a field.
post.description: Runs the SetText semantics action of a Compose field with value, or setText() of an EditText with the cursor at the end, then reads the tree. A Compose field that does not have the focus gets it first, as a user's tap gives it, so the keyboard opens: the settle then starts when the keyboard shows, or after 2000 ms when none does, as with a hardware keyboard, and after a keyboard it counts no two equal reads for 100 ms plus 300 ms times the animator duration scale, the time of the keyboard's animation, so the tree has the screen after it made room for the keyboard. The keyboard's animation can take longer than the default settle: send settle 1000 for a settled tree. Find a field by its test tag, or by its id; a label is often a node of its own beside the field. The selector looks in the unmerged tree, so a test tag or a text inside a clickable parent is found, and the action runs on the matched node or the nearest node above it that has it, as a tap on the text would. It acts as a user can, unless force is true: only in the window that has the focus and in the popups over it, such as a menu, which take no focus but get the touches inside them, also a popup that a popup with the focus opened, and only on a target with a part on the screen. post.summary: Scroll a list to an item, or by pixels.
post.description: With index, runs the ScrollToIndex semantics action of a Compose list, setSelection() of a ListView or GridView, or scrollToPosition() of a RecyclerView; with dx and dy, the ScrollBy action, or scrollBy() of a View. A ViewPager2, or its RecyclerView, turns its pages: index shows that page, and dx or dy turns to the nearest page, as a slow swipe does. A lazy list composes the rows in view only, so a row that is not in the tree needs a scroll first. The selector looks in the unmerged tree, so a test tag or a text inside a clickable parent is found, and the action runs on the matched node or the nearest node above it that has it, as a tap on the text would. It acts as a user can, unless force is true: only in the window that has the focus and in the popups over it, such as a menu, which take no focus but get the touches inside them, also a popup that a popup with the focus opened, and only on a target with a part on the screen. text.description: A text of the node, exactly, or its editable text.

contentDescription.description: A content description of the node, exactly.

id.description: The node's id from GET tree.

force.description: Act also on a node that a user can't tap now: in a window that does not have the focus and is not a popup on the one that has it, such as the activity under a dialog, or with no part on the screen. By default the tab refuses them.

merged.description: The tree of the response, merged or unmerged.

settle.description: After the action, read the tree on each frame from the next one until two reads in a row are the same and the window focus is at rest, for up to this many milliseconds, at least two frames: an animation that the action starts, such as a Compose scroll, moves nothing on its first frame.

dx.description: Pixels to scroll to the right; negative to the left. 0 when left out.

dy.description: Pixels to scroll down; negative up. 0 when left out.

windows.description: The app's windows, in the order the app added them: the activity, then the dialogs and popups over it.

merged.description: Whether the Compose nodes are the merged semantics tree.

density.description: The display density, pixels for each dp.

compose.description: Whether the app has Compose UI, so that the tree has the semantics nodes of its Compose hosts.

windowSource.description: How the tab found the windows: WindowInspector from API 29; WindowManagerGlobal before; or, when that failed, the started activities, without their dialogs and popups.

composeError.description: Why the tab could not read a Compose host's semantics tree, such as a Compose UI without a call that the tab makes. The host's View is in the tree without semantics nodes.

context.description: What the app's ScreenContextProvider returned, such as its navigation back stack: any JSON value, or null when the app registered none, it returned null, or it failed (see contextError).

contextError.description: Why context is null: the provider threw, or returned text that is not JSON.

ScreenWindow.description: A window of the app's process: an activity, or a dialog, popup, or bottom sheet over it.

id.description: The id of the window's root View, its first node.

type.description: The window type of the root View's WindowManager.LayoutParams, such as 1 for an activity and 2 for a dialog.

kind.description: The group of the type: activity for TYPE_BASE_APPLICATION; dialog for TYPE_APPLICATION and TYPE_APPLICATION_ATTACHED_DIALOG, which Dialog, DialogFragment, Compose's Dialog, and bottom sheet dialogs use; popup for the other sub-windows, which PopupWindow, Compose's Popup, menus, and spinners use; system for system window types, such as an overlay.

title.description: The window's title, such as the package and class of an activity.

hasWindowFocus.description: Whether the window has the window focus. A window of another app, such as a permission dialog or the chooser, can cover the app while the server still answers, and then no window of the app has the focus: read that window with uiautomator.

focusable.description: Whether the window can take the focus: false for a window with FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE, such as a popup that does not take the keys.

visible.description: Whether the window's root View is shown and the window is visible.

nodes.description: The window's nodes, each before its children, the children in the order of their parent.

ScreenNode.description: A node of a window: a classic View, or a Compose semantics node. A key that the node does not have is left out: a text, a role, a state that is not set, enabled when the node is enabled, and clickable, focused, password, and clipped when they are false.

id.description: v and a number for a View, which stays the same while the View lives; c, the number of the Compose host's View, a dot, and the semantics id for a Compose node, the same in the merged and the unmerged tree.

parent.description: The id of the node's parent. A window's first node has none. The parent of a Compose host's root semantics node is the host's View; the Views of an AndroidView in a Compose host follow the host's semantics nodes, with the host as their parent.

className.description: The class of a View, such as android.widget.Button. Compose nodes have none: see role.

resourceId.description: The resource name of a View's id, such as com.example:id/save. Generated ids have none.

testTag.description: A Compose node's Modifier.testTag, or a View's tag when it is a string. Every test tag is here, whether the app sets testTagsAsResourceId or not.

text.description: The node's text, one string for each text of a merged node, in order. A field's text is in editableText.

editableText.description: The text in a text field, which can be empty.

password.description: The node is a password field: editableText and text have one dot for each character, as the screen shows them.

role.description: A Compose node's Role, such as Button, Checkbox, Switch, RadioButton, Tab, Image, or DropdownList.

error.description: The error that a field shows, from Compose's error semantics or TextView.setError().

bounds.description: The node in its window, before any clipping.

screenBounds.description: The node on the screen, before any clipping.

visibleBounds.description: The part of the node that is on the screen after its parents and its window clip it; null when no part of it is, as a View that is INVISIBLE, a node of zero size, or a row scrolled out of view.

clipped.description: A parent or the window cuts the node, so only a part of it is on the screen.

selected.description: Whether the node is selected, as a tab: present for a Compose node that is selectable, and for a View only when it is selected.

toggle.description: The toggle state of a switch or check box: on, off, or indeterminate.

clickable.description: The node has a click action: OnClick is in actions.

actions.description: The semantics actions that drive the node, by their Compose names: OnClick, OnLongClick, SetText, PerformImeAction, ScrollBy, ScrollToIndex, PageUp, PageDown, PageLeft, PageRight, SetProgress, Expand, Collapse, and Dismiss. A View has OnClick when it is clickable, OnLongClick when it is long-clickable, SetText when it is an enabled EditText, ScrollBy when it can scroll, and ScrollToIndex when it is a ListView, a GridView, a RecyclerView, or a ViewPager2.

collection.description: A Compose list or grid: how many rows and columns it has, or null when it does not say.

Rect.description: A rectangle in pixels: left and top inside it, right and bottom just outside.

ScrollRange.description: The scroll position of a node on one axis, in pixels.

value.description: How far the node is scrolled.

max.description: How far it can scroll; null when the node does not say, as a View that is not a scroll container's.

reverse.description: Whether the node scrolls in reverse, as a list that starts at its end.

forward.description: Whether it can scroll further forward: down or right, or up or left when reverse.

Settle.description: How a settle wait ended. Present only when the request asked for one.

settled.description: Whether two reads on consecutive frames were the same and the window focus was at rest. false when the time was over first, and the tree is the last read, as while a window of another app has the focus.

frames.description: How many frames the tab read after the first read.

error.description: Machine error type, e.g. bad_request, not_found, timeout.

ScreenActionResult.description: What the action did, and the tree after it.

matched.description: The id of the node that the selector matched.

target.description: The id of the node whose action ran: the matched node, or the nearest node above it that has the action, as the clickable parent of a text.

handled.description: What the action returned: for a Compose node, its action's result; for a View, performClick()'s, which is false when the View has no click listener; true for a View's set-text and scroll.
